text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
- The opposition Solidarity trade union has urged its supporters to vote against a draft of Poland's new constitution prepared by parliament in a referendum on May 25.

- Poland's army will be reduced by 50,000 to 180,000 soldiers by 2004 and the number of divisions and centres of command will be cut to save money needed for modernisation, the country's new chief of staff Henry Szumski said during a meeting with President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- An undisclosed investor wants to buy a 49 percent stake in the state-owned PZU insurance firm worth 700 million zlotys by the end of July this year, the company said.

- Poland's state insurance supervision office (PUNU) has criticised the insurance firms' pricing of the OC civil liability policies for car owners, physicians and notaries because collected premiums do not cover damage payments, PUNU said.

- The state-owned CPN petrol distribution chain was Poland's biggest firm in 1996 regarding sales, according to a ranking of 100 companies produced by the Zycie Gospodarcze economic weekly. CPN's revenues were 12.62 billion zlotys. Petrochemia Plock, an oil refinery, came second with 10.469 billion zlotys and the PSE national power grid reported revenues of 10.318 billion zlotys.

- Sweden's Defence Minister Bjorn von Sydow and Poland's defence ministry officials have visited the WSK Mielec aircraft maker to discuss a possible cooperation between Sweden's SAAB aviation industry concern and WSK Mielec. SAAB and British Aerospace want to sell Poland its Jas-39 Gripen fighter jet.
- The Polish paper makers' exports totalled 1.2 billion zlotys ($438 million) in the first three quarters of last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The Polish cooperative banks' association (KZBS) has applied to Finance Minister Marek Belka for amending banking regulations to grant independant cooperative banks the same opportunities as those enjoyed by banks controlled by the state-owned BGZ agricultural sector bank.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The PZM shipping group shipped 6.2 million tonnes of freight in the first quarter of this year showing a slight upturn compared with the similar period in 1996, the firm said.

- Poland's industrial output in March grew by 6.6 percent compared with February while construction and assemblying production increased by 22.7 percent in the period, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Romet bicycle plant in Bydgoszcz, western Poland, sold 600,000 biycles on the domestic market last year and exported 180,000 bicycles, Romet's president Tomasz Zawadzki said. The plant produces 70 percent of the Polish-made bicycles.
ZYCIE
- Austrian firms have invested four billion schillings in Poland since 1990 mostly in the banking and construction sector, the government's foreign investment agency (PAIZ) said.
PARKIET
- Firms operating in Poland's banking, construction and food processing sectors have biggest growth prospects, a report by the HSBC James Capel said.
